ui.title_cos: Independence Title, Heritage Title of Austin, Austin Title, all in Austin
ui.title_call: Independence Title or Heritage Title of Austin
ui.law: Texas lets you assign a purchase contract, but you must tell the seller and your buyer in writing that you are selling your contract, not the house (Occupations Code 1101.0045). Texas foreclosures are non-judicial: houses sell at the courthouse on the first Tuesday of the month, about 21 days after notice.
ui.groups: "Austin Real Estate Investors", "Austin Real Estate Networking Club", "Texas Wholesale Deals"
ui.prefc: Estate: the appraisal district lists the owner as the estate of someone who died, so heirs are deciding what to do with the house. Life estate: an older owner kept the right to live there, but the tax mail now goes somewhere else. Every other lead is absentee: the tax bill is mailed to a different address than the house.
ui.buyers_note: Texas does not make sale prices public, so the county data cannot rank buyers by purchases. Look up any company owner on the Texas Comptroller search and call.
ui.buyers_empty: Texas does not make sale prices public, so the county data cannot show who is buying. Ask your title company who is closing cash deals.
ui.repairs: Repairs, Austin rough numbers per house: cosmetic 20-30k, kitchen+baths 35-60k, roof 12-22k, AC 8-14k, foundation 8-25k (clay soil), full gut 80-130k.
ui.sources: Travis Central Appraisal District parcel layer published by Travis County (owner, mailing address, market value, year built, deed date)
